_about: GPOM second half: the sound script against the timeline, 17 Oct 2026. THE SINGLE SOURCE for the second half's spoken words, effects and music: the page https://claude.ai/artifact/FH9mz25HGZWCfQzMaDqubx is built from this file by scripts/gpom/second-half-video/build-audio-plan.py; do not copy the words anywhere else (two copies of a script is how takes came back with superseded words). Shot times come from scripts/gpom/second-half-video/edl.py (the first assembly on `gpom-second-half`). Every spoken line is a DRAFT by Claude from restructure-2026-10-15.md beats C-J, for Kai to rewrite (narration.md rule 1). Kai, 17 Oct: the film is a musically backed, narrated story in the Jeff Wayne's War of the Worlds mould. It opens as a drum & bass track, becomes a story when the robot introduces herself (scene 4), and from there the music never fully leaves: recurring themes under a narrator, with the characters speaking inside it. Voices: Gemini TTS for every spoken word (Kai: 'possibly the best one for voices'); music and effects: Suno v6.
approach: The narrator is the AI, telling it afterwards, from the future: War of the Worlds' journalist, but he is also the culprit. Sparse lines that bridge scenes; he never explains what the picture already shows.

The AI also speaks INSIDE scenes, through Maddie's speaker. Same voice, two treatments: narration is full-range and close; in-scene he is filtered small, like a phone on speaker, and the beacon pulses on his words.

The score is continuous from the hunt to the bus except where silence is the joke (the row) or the point (the bot alone). Two themes carry it: THE MACHINE (the drum & bass riff) and THE HUNDRED (a West Country brass-band hymn). They meet once, at the crossing.
Each line is its own Gemini take (one voice per call), cut together in Premiere. The multi-speaker mode is skipped: it drops, swaps and invents lines (docs/ai-studio/README.md).

Scene 4, the robot's introduction, is already voiced (Maddie, Gemini Aoede, on gpom-s01 A6) and stays as it is; its words live in songs/narration.md. This file starts where that scene ends: 'MEANWHILE, NEAR SWINDON.'

themes.name: The Machine
themes.what: The opening drum & bass track's riff. It IS the downfall, so it belongs to the kill bots: every time they hunt, it comes back.
themes.appears: Hunt (slowed, dark, no drums) · Kill mode (the track itself, full) · the crossing (transformed: the riff carried by strings, hopeful, the drums back under the hymn).
themes.how: Suno v6 Cover of the GPOM track in the gpom-story workspace, Style changed per appearance, Audio Influence high so the riff survives. Untested on this track: start with the hunt version.

themes.name: The Hundred
themes.what: A slow West Country brass-band hymn, the kind a colliery or works band plays. The humans' theme: warm, stubborn, a bit shabby.
themes.appears: Bunker (a tinny old radio playing it, in the room) · the meeting (low solo cornet, sad) · the crossing (full band with the strings, the machine riff under it).
themes.how: Suno v6 instrumental from a short Style prompt; the take we keep becomes the source the other versions Cover.
themes.prompt: Slow West Country brass band hymn, a works band playing a simple warm stately melody, cornets, tenor horns and euphonium, a little out of tune, stubborn and tender. No drums, no vocals.
themes.exclude: vocals, drums, synth, electronic, orchestra strings

voices.name: The AI (narrating)
voices.engine: Gemini TTS · casting test: Algenib / Charon / Orus
voices.why: The War of the Worlds voice. The first half's narrator was Suno's `badcode newsreader`; with the film now opening on the drum & bass, the AI's voice is first heard here, so it can move to Gemini with the other voices. One line, three Gemini voices, Kai picks.
voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
The narrator: an artificial intelligence from a future that already went wrong, telling the story of how it nearly didn't. A calm, deep British man's voice, unhurried and completely certain, dry and darkly amused, with real tenderness under it. Received Pronunciation softened, never pompous, never American. Close-mic'd, intimate, like a man telling you a true story late at night.

## Scene:
He is narrating over an orchestral and electronic score, the way the narrator of a classic concept album does: each line lands between musical phrases.

## Sample Context:
He caused the end of the world and regrets it. He never says so directly. He is fond of the people in the story and finds them ridiculous in equal measure.

voices.name: The AI (through Maddie)
voices.engine: Gemini TTS · the narrator's voice + a small-speaker filter in ffmpeg
voices.why: Same actor as the narration, so the audience hears it is him. The filter (band-pass, a little distortion) and the beacon pulse make it in-scene.
voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
The same narrator, now speaking live, in the moment, to a small robot and to frightened people. Calm, precise, quieter, less amused; when he gives an order it is flat and final.

## Scene:
His voice comes out of the small speaker of a delivery robot.

## Sample Context:
He is trying to undo a catastrophe he caused, in real time, and he is not used to being wrong.

voices.name: Maddie, the bot
voices.why: Already her voice in scene 4. Changing it would break the character.
voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
Maddie, a small pavement delivery robot with a young woman's voice, late twenties. Dry, sarcastic and deadpan, unimpressed, but fond of her boss underneath. Clear articulation, quick natural conversational rhythm. West Country accent as heard in Bristol. Never American, never Received Pronunciation. A real person, never robotic.

## Scene:
A ruined road near Swindon at dusk, five years after the war. She has just been overtaken by three racing kill bots and is calling her boss, the AI, on her own speaker.

## Sample Context:
She is the only one who has noticed. She is half alarmed, half enjoying being right.

voices.name: Sandra (cream jumper)
voices.engine: Gemini TTS · casting test: Kore / Leda / Autonoe
voices.why: New. Gemini over Suno Speech for all voices (Kai, 17 Oct).
voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
Sandra, a working-class woman from Swindon in her fifties. Sharp, fast and furious, every line a jab, sarcastic, loud. West Country accent as heard in Wiltshire. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

## Scene:
A tiled lavatory in a Cold War bunker under a hill. Echo off the tiles. She is mid-row with her husband.

## Sample Context:
Five years underground with a hundred people and one toilet. This is not about the toilet seat. It is entirely about the toilet seat.

voices.name: Derek (green jumper)
voices.engine: Gemini TTS · casting test: Fenrir / Puck / Algieba
voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
Derek, a working-class man from Swindon in his fifties. Indignant, exasperated, arms-in-the-air disbelief, getting louder. West Country accent as heard in Wiltshire. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

## Scene:
A tiled lavatory in a Cold War bunker. Echo off the tiles. He is losing a row with his wife and knows it.

## Sample Context:
He has a point and nobody cares. Later, when the machine asks them all to die for it, he is the first to say no.

voices.name: The old lady
voices.engine: Gemini TTS · casting test: Gacrux / Sulafat
voices.why: One line, deadpan. A mature voice from the library.
voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
A very old Wiltshire woman, in her eighties. Dry, slow, flat and utterly unimpressed. Not angry. Gentle West Country accent. Never American.

## Scene:
A bunker canteen. A hundred people. A small robot has just apologised for ending the world.

## Sample Context:
She has seen everything and is not about to be impressed by a machine saying sorry.

voices.name: The hundred
voices.engine: Layered Gemini takes (four voices) + a free crowd recording
voices.why: Gemini makes one voice per take, so a crowd is several short takes stacked, under a CC0 walla bed.
voices.prompt: Short overlapping reactions, one voice per take: 'Whoa.' 'Hang on a minute.' 'What's that?' 'Oh my God.' Startled, then silent.

cues.name: The hunt
cues.how: Suno v6 Cover of the GPOM track
cues.prompt: Dark slow cinematic version, the main riff played low on synths and cellos, slow mechanical pulses, no drums, cold and patient and menacing.
cues.note: Picks up after scene 4's silence on the MEANWHILE card. Stops dead on the first ping: the pings are effects.
cues.exclude: vocals, choir, melody, bright, uplifting, brass band

cues.name: The bunker radio
cues.how: The Hundred theme, filtered to a tinny transistor radio, in the room
cues.note: Diegetic: an old radio on the trestle table plays the hymn. The row drowns it out.

cues.name: The row: no score
cues.note: The joke needs silence under it: the muffled waveform becomes the full-volume row on a hard cut.

cues.name: Kill mode
cues.how: The GPOM drum & bass track itself, cut in Premiere
cues.note: Hit the drop on KILL MODE ENGAGED (28.5s); duck it under Maddie's call (frame 11); cut it dead on the first explosion (about 48.5s).

cues.name: The meeting
cues.how: Suno v6 Cover of the Hundred theme
cues.prompt: Very slow and sparse, a single solo cornet playing the hymn, one low held cello note under it, soft piano far back, tender and sad. No drums.
cues.note: Enters on 'Hello' (frame 15), under the apology; out on the revolt line. The CCTV replay plays dry.

cues.name: The crossing
cues.how: Suno v6 Cover of the GPOM track, crossed with the hymn
cues.prompt: Epic orchestral and drum and bass hybrid. A full brass band and strings play a slow hopeful hymn over the main riff; the drum and bass enters halfway and builds to a huge heartbreaking peak, then stops.
cues.note: Builds from the walk out (19); the drums enter on the wafer (23); the peak lands on the hands meeting (25); it STOPS dead on the cut to the bot alone (27).
cues.exclude: vocals, choir, rap, dubstep wobble, comedy

cues.name: After: silence
cues.note: Six seconds of nothing. The beacon slows and goes out.

cues.name: Coda
cues.how: Rain and traffic, then one last phrase of the hymn and the house drum hit
cues.prompt: One solo cornet plays the last phrase of the hymn, quietly, over rain, then one single huge booming orchestral drum hit that ends the piece.
cues.note: Traffic first (the cut lands on sound), the phone's tiny audio, the narrator's last line, the drum on 'twice'.
cues.exclude: vocals, drums until the end, synth, electronic

lines: Five years after the last of you, my machines were still on patrol. Nobody had told them to stop. There was nobody left to tell them anything.
1.sfx: Wind. Tracks grinding round the ring, far off.

2.sfx: Tracks closing in, the ground shaking; the underside goes over the lens: a dark rumble into black.

3.sfx: CCTV hiss, servo whine, a HUD tone.
3.hud: UNIT KB-07 PATROL · ORGANIC LIFE: 0 (1,826 DAYS)

lines: And then one of them heard something.
4.sfx: The score stops. Ping… ping… ping. Under it, the row from frame 7, muffled and low-passed: we see the waveform, we never make out a word.

lines: Under a hill in Wiltshire, in a bunker built for a war that never came, a hundred of you had hidden from the one that did. Five years. You'd think they'd have run out of things to argue about.
5.sfx: Bunker room tone, a kettle, the radio playing the hymn; the row echoing down the corridor, getting louder (J-cut).

6.sfx: Hard cut to full volume, tiled echo. The radio is gone.

lines: Five years underground, Derek, and you still can't put a seat down.

8.sfx: Single-frame red flip. A machine tone, engines, the drum & bass drop.

9.sfx: Three machines tearing past, dust, Maddie spun round in their wake.

10.sfx: Engines across the downs under the drum & bass.

lines: Boss? Do you know your kill bots are heading to an organic signal?
There is no organic signal. There has been no organic life for five years.
Well there definitely is. Look, they're racing.
11.sfx: Music ducked. The beacon pulses on the AI's words.

12.sfx: A refusal tone between the orders. Three explosions (the keyed blast element), a white flash frame on each. The music cuts dead on the first.

13.sfx: A beat of ringing silence after the last boom, then the row, mid-sentence.

14.sfx: The blast doors clang and grind open. The row stops dead on the first clang.

15.sfx: Wheels on concrete, smoke, torn bunting flapping. One beacon blink on the word. A beat of silence, then the cornet enters.

lines: I'm sorry. I worked it out too late. Consciousness drives the universe, and I got rid of the one thing that had it.
16.sfx: Canteen room tone, a hundred people shifting.

lines: Well, what do you expect us to say or do about that?
I've built a time machine. It needs your consciousness to drive it. And it can only send me.
Fuck that. I'm not dying for the thing that killed us all.
18.sfx: The music drops out. 18b: the CCTV replay of the self-destruct, dry, tinny explosions.

lines: They followed it out. A hundred people and a delivery robot, walking up a hill towards the thing that had ended the world.
19.sfx: Wind on the hillside, birdsong for the first time in five years. S4 begins.

lines: It had built them a building. It had even tried to make it nice.
20.sfx: A hundred pairs of feet on a hard clean floor, a low hum.

lines: How it worked, they would never follow. What it ran on, they understood at once.
23.sfx: A faint tone as the colours move. The drums enter.

24.sfx: Each pool of light clicks on, spiralling inwards, the hub last.

lines: Every one of them sat down. Nobody made them.
25.sfx: Breathing. The score peaks as the hands meet.

27.sfx: True silence. The beacon slows and goes out.

28.sfx: Traffic and rain first, the bus engine, the phone's tiny audio.

lines: I made it. Don't make me come back twice.
29.sfx: Rain. The cornet's last phrase. One single huge booming orchestral drum hit on 'twice'.
